current_answer: Jev is TypeSafe AI’s hosted model for bounded Choice, Score and Noul judgments; application code owns validation, policy, permissions, action and fallback. Direct-source checks on 25 September 2026 found several independent open-weight Jev-like models and numerous project integration paths, but did not verify TypeSafe Jev weights in public sources, model parity, a current production customer deployment or independent workload performance. Direct TypeSafe lists $0.042 per million input tokens and free output; gateway billing and access differ, with Vercel’s promotion/price conflict unresolved.

catalogue_card.question: What can I build with Jev, what alternatives exist, and where can I use it at what cost?
catalogue_card.text: Compare evidence-labelled use cases, independent model and interface alternatives, direct-code and README project integrations, and dated provider routes. The workload protocol has no results; audit the selected account and data terms before a pilot.

summary: Choice, Score and Noul return bounded decisions; code still owns policy and side effects.
Kev, CLM, Laya, Jeff and OpenDecision are independent Jev-like alternatives with different weight, API and licence boundaries; they are not TypeSafe Jev weights.
Numerous Jev integration paths were documented or inspected, but none of the audited rows independently verified a current production customer deployment.
Direct TypeSafe lists jev-1.13.0, $0.042/M input, free output, dynamic limits and a text-only direct API.
OpenRouter, Cloudflare, Vercel and Netlify have different endpoints, account terms and pricing; Vercel current charge is unresolved at the promotion boundary.
The preceding-24-hour monitor found AgentRun and two arXiv papers within the window; X, TikTok, native search surfaces and some time metadata were inaccessible.
No authenticated call or independent benchmark was run; the workload protocol remains unfilled.
uncertainty: TypeSafe Jev weights were not publicly located or published in checked sources; this is not a legal proprietary-status conclusion.
No same-workload independent comparison establishes Jev-like model parity; Laya licence and base-model terms need checks.
No audited project was independently verified as a currently operating production Jev product, although direct code and documented integrations exist.

Account eligibility, credits, live quota, data controls and actual bill were not checked for any route. Vercel pricing/promotion conflict, Netlify credit conversion and Cloudflare dashboard rate remain unresolved.
X current posts and TikTok were not adequately accessible; the 24-hour scan is bounded, not exhaustive.
No independent Jev accuracy, calibration, latency, safety or production threshold was measured.
